question: Should OpenClaw expose a public reset-start prompt override, and if so should it live under top-level `session`, `agents.defaults`, per-agent config, or a broader reset-greeting policy surface?
rationale: Adding a new prompt/config key changes a public configuration contract, and repository policy treats new config surfaces as high-bar product decisions rather than automatic bug-fix work.

options.title: Approve one canonical reset-start surface
options.body: Define a single full-replacement prompt override with documented global and per-agent precedence, preserving the current built-in prompt as the unset fallback.

options.title: Fold into broader reset-greeting policy
options.body: Handle this together with model selection and suppress-greeting requests so users get one coherent reset-start configuration family.

options.title: Decline new config surface
options.body: Keep reset startup behavior owned by the built-in prompt and existing startupContext mechanisms, leaving persona-specific workarounds outside the public config schema.

recommendation.title: Approve one canonical reset-start surface
recommendation.body: Define a single full-replacement prompt override with documented global and per-agent precedence, preserving the current built-in prompt as the unset fallback.
